A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same single-cell perturbation study, renamed from Unlasting to Doloris. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v2 reports original prediction experiments on Adamson, Norman, and sci-Plex3 in Tables 1–2, plus component ablations in Figure 6.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark and ablation results, together with gene-activation prediction, diversity, sampling-step, and dimensionality analyses in Figures 2 and 5–8.

M1.justification: The dual diffusion bridge and masked reconstruction loss remain, but important components change. v2 Section 3.4 uses learnable gene embeddings and knockout masking; v3 Appendix A.7 uses frozen PCA-derived expression features and extracts perturbed-gene embeddings after GAT propagation. v2 Appendix A.2 thresholds and aggregates mask predictions, whereas v3 Section 3.6 and Appendix A.11 select similar training-cell subsets, sample real masks, and override entries using 0.05/0.95 probability thresholds.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Adamson single-gene perturbations, Norman double-gene perturbations, and sci-Plex3 unseen drug–cell-type–dosage combinations and OOD drugs. The new diagnostics examine this retained coverage. The sci-Plex3 drug-count description changes from 187 to 188, but no additional drug or distinct evaluation scenario is identified.

E2.justification: v3 adds the linear baseline to both genetic comparisons and BioLord to the sci-Plex3 comparison. GraphVCI is removed from the Adamson portion of Table 1 but retained in molecular comparisons. ScLambda already appears in v2 Table 1 and is not a newly introduced benchmark comparator.

E3.justification: v3 adds RMSE throughout Tables 1–2, changes the stated normalization maximum from the test set to the training set, and reduces Adamson training from 20,000 to 10,000 steps. New analyses introduce sampling-step settings of 1, 30, 50, and 70 and HVG subsets from 50 to 2,000 genes. These are reported protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish which earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds activation-probability validation, an intra-class-distance diversity comparison, sampling-step sensitivity, and an analysis of SNR versus gene count (Figures 2, 5, 7, and 8). The control-information, latent, and masking ablations remain, but the molecular GRN ablation is removed. The illustrative bimodal-expression case also changes from CREB1 in v2 Figure 5 to ZNF326 in v3 Figure 4.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark values with ± quantities without specifying their statistical meaning, repeated-run counts, or seeds. v3 introduces no confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure. Additional entries and changed ± values retain the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Many benchmark values are revised and RMSE and comparator results are added. For example, the proposed method's Adamson all-gene E-distance changes from 0.8426 to 0.4682, while sci-Plex3 all-gene EMD changes from 0.0255 to 0.0265. ScLambda's Adamson DE20 EMD changes from 0.0904 to 0.0914. New findings include declining relative SNR with additional genes and diminishing sampling gains beyond 30 steps. Method and protocol revisions prevent interpreting these score changes as established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds computational-cost reasoning, deriving costs of 2N+1 per sample and (N+1)kn+mN with reused control latents. Appendix A.5 introduces the between-condition/within-condition SNR and relative-SNR definitions. Existing diffusion and distribution-distance mathematics is largely retained or restated; no substantial theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: The central claims of unpaired prediction through dual diffusion bridges, diversity-preserving masking, unseen-perturbation generalization, and superior benchmark performance remain. v3 foregrounds masking as a standalone contribution and drops the novel-GRN and data-augmentation emphasis. The evaluation-metric contribution disappears from the abstract and contribution list but remains in the body and conclusion, so it is not wholly withdrawn.

C2.justification: v2's standalone interpretation of DDIB as data augmentation is removed. v3 adds a Hurdle-model interpretation, a biological argument for informative zeros, and an explanation of why independent mask sampling can violate global coherence. Section 3.4 explicitly distinguishes Gaussian conditioning noise from an assumption of Gaussian expression. Baseline interpretations also shift toward sparsity, mean collapse, and limitations of linear distributional modeling.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies AdamW, learning rate 0.001, A100 80 GB hardware, Norman's training budget, the sci-Plex3 30% condition holdout, mask thresholds, and PCA-based feature initialization, and provides code-access information. Conversely, v2's 5,000/2,000 benchmark gene counts, explicit GRN-construction rule and associated settings, and MLP architecture description are no longer documented. Newly disclosed settings alone do not establish changes to the underlying experiments.

R1.justification: v3 removes the standalone GRN/foundation-model and molecular-representation review and several associated references. It adds positioning around linear baselines, BioLord, ScLambda, PRESCRIBE, high-dimensional statistics, and biologically informative zeros. Appendix A.10 newly distinguishes unseen-perturbation prediction from optimal-transport pairing, including CINEMA-OT. These changes substantially revise the research context beyond the switch to author–year citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and methodology are extensively rewritten and reorganized. The methods now separately explain source modeling, target modeling, masking, inference, and implementation; masking moves into the main text, while revised perturbation encoding appears in the appendix. Appendices A–C are reorganized into A.1–A.11. The title, method name, author information, and conference formatting also change.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the framework overview, removes v2's detailed architecture and data-augmentation diagrams, and adds diversity, activation-prediction, sampling, and SNR displays. Table 1 gains RMSE columns; Table 2 is transposed and adds ranking colors and a score-difference column. Figure 6 changes from grouped bars to line plots, and several displays become compact figures beside text.

improvement.justification: The added linear/BioLord comparisons, RMSE results, and direct masking and sampling analyses make the empirical case more informative. Specifying training-only scaling also corrects v2's stated dependence on test statistics, although rerunning the experiments is not established. These benefits are tempered by removal of the GRN ablation and some architecture and gene-count details, while Appendix A.11 leaves reference-subset selection underspecified. Together, the evidence supports a limited net quality improvement.
